item.title: Why Your LED Strip Flickers: PWM, Power and Ground Explained
item.description: An LED strip that flickers, dims unevenly or shows random colours is telling you one of four things: not enough power, too much voltage drop, a data signal that is too weak, or a ground that is not shared. Each has a different fix, and each is measurable in minutes.

item.title: Fixing Relay Chatter When Switching AC Loads from an ESP32
item.description: A relay that buzzes, clicks repeatedly, or resets your ESP32 is almost never a broken relay. It is a power, isolation or snubber problem. Fix those three and the circuit becomes as reliable as any commercial smart switch.

item.title: Driving a DC Motor from an ESP32 with a Low-Side MOSFET
item.description: An ESP32 pin can only supply a few milliamps, so it can never power a motor directly. A logic-level MOSFET turns the pin into a safe, fast electronic switch and lets you control speed with PWM.

item.title: ESP32 Won't Wake from Deep Sleep: Causes and Fixes
item.description: Deep sleep is the single most useful feature of a battery ESP32 — and the one that trips up the most people. If your board never wakes, wakes instantly, or drains a 18650 in three days, one of the six causes below is almost certainly the reason.

item.title: Why Your ESP32 Wi-Fi Keeps Dropping (and How to Fix It Permanently)
item.description: An ESP32 that connects once, then drops, reconnects, or loses packets is rarely a faulty chip. In almost every case, the cause is one of five things: weak power, bad antenna placement, wrong Wi-Fi power-save settings, a missing reconnect routine, or interference from your own 2.4 GHz network.
